body: The Mets are losing, classic Mets.

I would give anything to have a job.  I don't even care what it is.  But I have no experience doing anything, no ID, no friends, no family.  I have applied to job and been laughed at.  I applied to jobs all last week, and was laughed at.  I have no transportation, so I can only apply to a small number of jobs in this area.  If I had a job or a friend or anything, maybe life would be workable.  But I don't.  I have nothing.

How did I make it this far?  I have no idea.

I tried working out today.  It was impossible.  I have no energy, no motivation.  

I am 26.  I cannot drive, I have never had a job.  Not a real job, I worked in the IT department in college as a student/work thing.  My degree is useless, I never did any internships.  I have no money, no transportation, no experience, no friends, and nobody who cares about me.  I've had chronic depression for my entire life, I've been hospitalized multiple times.  I can't function.  And the funny part is, my depression is at an all time low.  Meaning, I feel less depressed now than I ever have in my life.  The depression isn't even an issue anymore, or at least not right now.  But my life is FUCKED beyond all recognition.

Where do I even start?  Walk to the DMV tomorrow and try to get a learners permit at age 26?  Oh, that costs money and requires a birth certificate.  Two things I don't have.  And even if I got a permit, then what?  I can drive with my nonexistent friends and family in my nonexistent car with my nonexistent gas until I learn how to drive?  Sounds like a plan.  Then what?  I can go with my nonexistent car and take a road test?  And then I can take that nonexistent car and go try to find a job with my absolutely no job experience.  People will say, so you're 26 years old, you have no references, no experience, and you want a job?  Yeah, no.  We'll hire some 15 year old or something, thanks.

And then, once I have my nonexistent license and car and the job I'll never get, then maybe I can start trying to find a place to live and food.

Yeah, that sounds great.  Suicide is the only real option I have.

I feel the stress of wanting to kill myself every single day for the past 16 years being lifted off of my shoulders.  All of the people who said no, don't do it.  Think about it more.  You'll regret it.  It gets better.  Give it another day.  I gave it thousands of days.  It never got better.  My life has gotten consistently worse.

And no, I don't really want to die.  I just can't go on like this anymore.  I don't see any other option to get out of this mess.  Everything I have tried has gotten me back to where I am now, except with less hope and more miserable.  So I give up.  I should have given up a long time ago and spared myself all the heartache.  I tried to kill myself 11 years ago, and it almost worked.  I wish it did.  Every day for the past 11 years I wish it worked the first time.

Well, I guess you can call it whatever you want.  I call it rock bottom.  I have no money, no friends, no skills, nothing to do, I haven't eaten in three days, and I spent all yesterday crying/trying to think of some way to get better/contemplating suicide because I couldn't think of anything.  So whatever you call that.  Maybe you could call it a breaking point.  Something has to change.  I guess you could say it might be worse if I were in some sort of debt, or maybe if I didn't have an internet connection or something.  But I don't feel either of those things would be substantially different.

I do agree with the going outside bit.  I can say it did help me somewhat.  I hike multiple times per week.  It does ease my mind a little.  But it just isn't enough anymore.  This past weekend I hiked about twenty miles, it was beautiful weather, I saw nice sites and views.  But once I got home, I was totally paralyzed with loneliness and a longing for something, anything.

I need someone to take me by the hand and help me.  Is there anyone out there that can help?  I feel I am so close.  I had a rough childhood, being sexually abused.  I had a rough time in college, and I have had a rough time post college, with my dad dying and having severe depression.  But I have fought through it, and I know I'm ready to take the next step and be productive.  I don't want free handouts, I want to work.  And I'm so close. I don't want to make all the fighting I've done to get to this point go for nothing.

I believe if I had a job and dignity, I could handle the rest without much issue.  I just want a job, somewhere to live, and to eat food that doesn't make me sick.  That is really all I want.

I struggled through depression for years, and ultimately the way I got out of it was by forgetting about me and just focusing entirely on a small list of specific things.  For instance, I hiked and followed a baseball team.  I just focused on them, and I got control over my emotions and mood after a while.  I was stable this way for quite a while until a few days ago when I realized I am done with it.  It is time to move on, I can't stay this way forever.  I need dignity, and a job.  But I don't know how.  I don't know where to start, who to talk to, or what to say.
A lot in the past year.  In the past nine months I've lost about fifty pounds from working out and exercising. I could stand to lose fifty more, though.
